claims.label: Just Compensation Valuation
claims.note: Routine comparable-sales-driven disputes ran ~50-100% above the initial offer in the research sample.

claims.label: Regulatory Taking (Penn Central/Lucas)
claims.note: Rarely succeeds absent a near-total wipeout of economic value; when it does, damages tend toward full pre-regulation value.

outcome.description: After a three-day February 2021 non-jury trial the Montgomery County court found the property's fair market value at the taking was $667,000: $1,100,000 less $175,000 for demolition and $258,200 for Act 2 remediation, with no environmental-stigma deduction and no Lease in effect. Judgment of December 16, 2021 awarded $517,000 in just compensation plus $4,000 fee reimbursement ($521,000). The Board of View had awarded $1,000,000; the owner's appraiser said $2,100,000 and the Township's about $425,000 after deductions. The Commonwealth Court affirmed on October 19, 2023. Amount used is the fair market value found (total compensation, of which the $150,000 estimated just compensation was already paid).
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed. The $517,000 judgment equals the $667,000 value less the $150,000 paid in January 2017; the opinion does not say so expressly, but the arithmetic matches and it follows the Board of View's 'less the $150,000 already paid' format. The $4,000 is a statutory fee reimbursement.

source.caseName: Tank Car Corporation of America v. Springfield Township (consolidated cross-appeals)
source.court: Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania, on appeal from the Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas (non-jury trial on appeal from the Board of View)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from Part I, Factual and Procedural History: the property and its contamination, the EPA cleanup and cap, the school-bus Lease and the Township's injunction action, the declaration of taking, the $150,000 estimated just compensation and the Board of View's $1,000,000 award (an interim figure), footnote 2 (Act 2), and Part I.D-E: each appraiser's methods, figures and deductions (owner's Barth: $2,100,000 reconciled; Township's Lukens: $750,000 before deductions, $175,000 demolition, Penn E&R's $258,200 Act 2 estimate plus 10% contingency, 20% stigma) and the parties' evidence on whether the Lease was in effect. Record citations ('Id. at ...a') are kept as they appear. Removed: the opening paragraph (judgment amount and affirmance), footnotes 1 and 3-5 and markers, Barth's six numbered comparable sales and the Swedeland Road comparable, Part I.F (the trial court's findings: value $1,100,000 less demolition and Act 2 costs, no stigma deduction, no Lease) and everything after it.
